key_insight: The paper introduces a sound runtime verification framework for AI agents that bounds policy-violation probability even when predicates or transitions are probabilistic and correlated.
engineering_relevance: It enables more practical security monitoring for agentic systems by handling uncertain tool outputs and PII/declassifier failures without relying on unrealistic independence assumptions.
method: Formulate probabilistic policy verification in Datalog using distributionally robust optimization.
Compute sound upper bounds on violation probability under arbitrary predicate correlations.
Target runtime monitoring for AI agents in complex digital environments.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports evaluation on standard benchmarks for terminal and tool-calling agents, showing better security-utility trade-offs than prior art while preserving rigorous violation bounds.
watch_item: The approach provides upper bounds, so practical deployment may be limited by conservatism and the cost of integrating robust probabilistic monitoring into real agent pipelines.
paper_title: Efficient and Sound Probabilistic Verification for AI Agents
